prerequisites: Having studied Physics in the last year of high school
Prior mathematical knowledge of vector calculus, trigonometry, and derivation and integration of single-variable functions

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the physical-mathematical description of particle motion and know the magnitudes that quantify it.
Understand the laws and theorems that relate the motion of particles to the causes that provoke it.
Understand the concepts and principles necessary for the study of heat exchange processes in closed systems of ideal gases.
Correctly handle the recommended physical symbology, both in terms of magnitudes and units.
Learn and apply problem-solving strategies related to the different contents of the subject.
Acquire skills related to laboratory work and the treatment of measurements and errors.

syllabus_topics: Physical magnitudes. Treatment of measurement errors.
Thermometry and calorimetry. First principle of thermodynamics.
teaching_methods: Exposition and defense of problems, works, projects
Use of simulation software and/or experimental data processing
Analysis of results and preparation of practice reports
assessment_rules: For continuous assessment, the final grade (NFO) is calculated as NFO = EvC + (1 – EvC/10) × CGO, where EvC is the continuous assessment score and CGO is the global exam score. A minimum of 3.5 points (out of 10) is required in the global exam (CGO) to apply this formula. A minimum global score of 2.0 points out of 5.5 is required in continuous assessment activities; failing this results in a zero for continuous assessment. If continuous assessment is lost or opted out, the final grade (NFE) is solely the global exam score (CGE). Any final grade below 5.0 points results in a FAIL.
